headline: Why Salesforce Stock Slumped on Tuesday
summary: Salesforce shares fell over 2% on Tuesday as part of a broader software sector selloff triggered by IBM's weak earnings guidance. IBM CEO Arvind Krishna attributed the underperformance to customers shifting technology spending from software to hardware (servers and storage) due to AI infrastructure buildout and anticipated price increases. This trend poses headwinds for software companies like Salesforce despite their historical strength.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock declined 2.13% on Tuesday due to broader software sector weakness. While Salesforce itself had no direct negative news, investor sentiment turned bearish on the entire software segment following IBM's weak guidance and revelation that customers are shifting capex priorities away from software solutions toward hardware infrastructure.

Company issued weak preliminary quarterly earnings with only 1% revenue growth and 5% non-GAAP net income growth, both missing analyst expectations. CEO attributed underperformance to customers prioritizing hardware spending over software due to AI buildout and supply-constrained price increases, triggering a broader software sector selloff.
